handoff.purpose: Module docstring, imports, junk/cross-language filters, git wrapper, linked-worktree detection.

symbols.name: _IDENTIFIER_RE
symbols.note: Regex for identifier name shape: allows unicode letters/digits/underscore and optional leading/embedded $.

symbols.name: _JUNK_KEYWORDS
symbols.note: Frozenset of reserved words and node-text markers considered junk labels.

symbols.name: _LANGUAGE_FAMILIES
symbols.note: Maps c/cpp to c_cpp and javascript/typescript to js_ts.

symbols.name: _language_family
symbols.note: Returns family key for a language name; None stays None.

symbols.name: _is_junk_label
symbols.note: Returns True if name is not a valid identifier or is in _JUNK_KEYWORDS.

symbols.name: MINT_CONFIRM_THRESHOLD
symbols.note: Threshold for confirmations before a minted task leaves quarantine.

symbols.name: DEFAULT_MINT_STORE_PATH
symbols.note: Path to the minted tasks JSON store.

symbols.name: _git
symbols.note: Runs git in repo_root; returns stdout on success, None on any failure.

symbols.name: _is_linked_worktree
symbols.note: Detects linked worktree by checking .git file and gitdir pointer.

claims.text: Every task in daedalus.eval.tasks today was hand-picked by a human who then verified the pick by running semantic_slice -- circular, because the label is graded against the exact process that produced it (see tasks.py:1-8).
claims.why: No reference to tasks.py contents in this chunk.

claims.text: This module mints must_include labels from a source that has no opinion about the import graph at all: a byte-for-byte diff of what actually changed on disk, either a landed offload edit or a real git commit.
claims.why: Minting logic is in _mint_from_diffs, not in this chunk.

claims.text: *** DO NOT expand a minted must_include through graph.callees / the import closure -- here or anywhere downstream of this module. *** ... must_include is ONLY: symbols whose extracted source differs between before and after, plus symbols that were added or removed outright. Nothing transitive, ever -- not even "just one hop of direct callees".
claims.why: Enforcement is in _mint_from_diffs (later chunk) and downstream modules not visible here.

claims.text: Minted tasks land with "tier": "quarantine" and "label_provenance": "independent_diff" and are barred from any go/no-go recall number until confirm_task has been called on them MINT_CONFIRM_THRESHOLD times.
claims.why: No minting or confirm_task code in this chunk; MINT_CONFIRM_THRESHOLD defined here but enforcement elsewhere.

claims.text: SCOPE: a changed file is eligible as target OR as a label source only if it appears in cached_index(repo)["modules"] -- the exact membership test slice.py's own neighborhood expansion uses (rel in modules, slice.py around line 225; that is THE scope boundary, not a second opinion about it).
claims.why: No cached_index usage in this chunk; slice.py reference not verifiable.

claims.text: A minified dist/*.js build artifact is real text with hundreds of mechanical "symbols" but was never part of the project the slicer reasons about -- scoring recall against it measures nothing, and it is usually not even indexed (dist is a hard-excluded dir, see structcore/index.py _IGNORE_DIRS).
claims.why: No index.py reference in this chunk.

claims.text: Changed files that fail this test are recorded in skipped_out_of_scope on the diagnostics returned alongside the task (and on the task itself when one is minted) -- never silently dropped.
claims.why: Diagnostics and task construction are in _mint_from_diffs, not this chunk.

claims.text: CROSS-FILE ONLY: must_include never contains a symbol defined in the file chosen as target. ... A commit/edit where only one in-scope file has any diffed symbols therefore has no valid label source at all: it mints nothing rather than minting a label=[] task (harness._recall returns a vacuous 1.0 for an empty must_include, which would be worse than not minting). THE SAME GUARD APPLIES AFTER LABEL HYGIENE BELOW: ... _mint_from_diffs re-checks non-emptiness once, after filtering, and mints nothing (with a reason) if nothing survives.
claims.why: All enforcement is in _mint_from_diffs (later chunk); harness._recall not visible.

claims.text: JUNK: a diffed name that fails _is_junk_label ... never becomes a must_include entry -- dropped names land in labels_filtered_junk (sorted).
claims.why: _is_junk_label defined here, but filtering logic and labels_filtered_junk are in _mint_from_diffs.

claims.text: This list is deliberately narrow: a name that is a real, commonly-used identifier in even one supported language (delete as a Python/Django method, New as a Go exported constructor) is NOT junk just because it is also a reserved word in some other language.
claims.why: _JUNK_KEYWORDS excludes delete, new, default, case, switch, static, of, in; _is_junk_label is case-sensitive, so New/Default/Case/Switch are not junk.

claims.text: CROSS-LANGUAGE: a label may only come from a file whose language FAMILY (_language_family(languages.spec_for(...).name)) matches the TARGET's ... Families group languages the slicer's own import graph routinely crosses (a C++ file and its own .h; a .ts file and the .js it imports) -- those are NOT cross-language for this filter's purposes ... Filtered names land in labels_filtered_cross_language (sorted).
claims.why: _language_family and _LANGUAGE_FAMILIES defined here, but the filter application and labels_filtered_cross_language are in _mint_from_diffs.

claims.text: FLOOR-TRIPPING LABEL SOURCE EXCLUSION: sensitivity.secret_floor_rule is run against every anchor CANDIDATE's current content before target selection. A file that trips the floor is dropped from the ANCHOR POOL (recorded in skipped_secret_floor) ... AND from label consideration ... Filtered names land in labels_filtered_secret_floor (sorted).
claims.why: secret_floor_rule is imported, but usage is in _mint_from_diffs.

claims.text: Name-shape check: unicode-aware (a non-ASCII identifier -- café -- is legal Python/JS/etc and must not be treated as noise just for using non-ASCII letters) and allows a leading/embedded $ (legal anywhere in a JS/TS identifier, e.g. Angular's $scope) on top of the universal letter/digit/underscore identifier shape.
claims.why: Regex r"^(?:[^\W\d]|\$)[\w$]*$" allows unicode letters (in Python re, \w is unicode by default), digits, underscore, and $ at start or embedded.

claims.text: Keyword check: deliberately NARROW, and case-SENSITIVE. Real reserved words are fixed-case in every language here (always lowercase) -- a PascalCase match (New, Default, Case, Switch) is essentially never grammar-recovery noise and near-always a real exported identifier ... The set below is further limited to words that are reserved in EVERY supported language and implausible as a real symbol name in any of them -- unlike new/delete/default/case/switch/static/of/in, which are ordinary, common identifiers in at least one supported language (Python has none of these as keywords at all) and were previously flagged as junk regardless of case, silently deflating recall for real symbols like a Python/Django delete view method or a Go New constructor.
claims.why: _JUNK_KEYWORDS is all lowercase and excludes new, delete, default, case, switch, static, of, in; _is_junk_label does a case-sensitive membership check.

claims.text: CROSS-LANGUAGE FAMILY (label hygiene, lane A1): languages the slicer's own import graph routinely crosses, so a label source in the "other" member is NOT cross-language for recall purposes -- imports.py resolves a C/C++ #include "foo.h" regardless of whether the includer is .c or .cpp (.h is its own LanguageSpec, name "c"), and a .ts file's import can resolve straight to a co-located .js module. Every LanguageSpec name NOT listed here maps to its own singleton family (its prior, unchanged behavior) -- this is purely additive grouping, not a relaxation of the filter for any language pair not named below.
claims.why: The mapping is present, but the claim about imports.py behavior is not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: The cross-language filter's equality key for lang_name -- see _LANGUAGE_FAMILIES above. None (no LanguageSpec) stays None and therefore never equals any real family, same fail-closed behavior as before this grouping existed.
claims.why: Function returns None for None input; otherwise returns mapped family or the language name itself.

claims.text: True if name cannot be a real symbol label -- see the JUNK FILTER comment above. Checked name-shape-first (a non-identifier like <anonymous> never reaches the keyword set at all). The keyword check is intentionally case-SENSITIVE (see the comment above _JUNK_KEYWORDS for why) -- name is matched as-is, never lowercased.
claims.why: Function first checks _IDENTIFIER_RE.match(name); if it fails, returns True without checking keywords. Then checks name in _JUNK_KEYWORDS, which is case-sensitive.

claims.text: Below this many independent confirmations a mint stays quarantined and is excluded from go/no-go. Rationale: a SINGLE diff-derived label can be a false positive from mechanical noise our line-based unit diff can't see through ... Three independent mints landing on the same must_include set is a defensible floor before the label influences a headline number, while staying low enough to actually accumulate from real (comparatively infrequent) commit/offload activity instead of never firing.
claims.why: The constant is defined, but the gating logic is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Persisted mint store -- the load path that was missing entirely before this fix. Without it, mint_task_from_landed_edit/mint_from_commit returned in-memory dicts that evaporated at process exit and daedalus.eval.tasks.TASKS stayed a hardcoded literal forever ... Sibling of harness.py's DEFAULT_BASELINE_PATH: same directory, same "JSON file, sorted keys, schema-versioned" contract. Absence of the file (a fresh checkout, or a repo where nothing has ever been minted) means "nothing minted yet", not an error -- see load_minted_tasks.
claims.why: The constant is defined, but load_minted_tasks and minting functions are not in this chunk; harness.py not visible.

claims.text: Run git in repo_root; stdout on success, None on ANY failure (missing git, not a repo, bad ref, timeout, non-zero exit). Minting must degrade to "nothing minted", never raise -- a caller looping over commits or landed edits cannot be allowed to die on the first unreadable one.
claims.why: Function catches OSError and subprocess.SubprocessError, returns None; checks returncode != 0 and returns None; otherwise returns proc.stdout.

claims.text: True if repo_root is a git LINKED WORKTREE, not a primary checkout. ... Detection is the git on-disk contract, not a path heuristic: git worktree add writes .git as a FILE holding a gitdir: pointer, whereas a primary checkout has .git as a DIRECTORY. ... The pointer alone is NOT enough ... a SUBMODULE also has .git as a gitdir: file ... Nor is the pointer's PATH enough ... So the admin directory the pointer resolves to is inspected STRUCTURALLY ... commondir and gitdir together appear only in the linked-worktree admin layout. Requiring BOTH means an unreadable or unexpected target fails toward "not ephemeral", i.e. toward minting -- which is the correct direction for a false negative here ...
claims.why: The function's beginning is present and consistent with the claims so far (checks .git is file, reads pointer, checks gitdir: prefix), but the structural inspection of the admin directory is in the remainder of the function, not in this chunk.

observations.what: Module docstring contains extensive behavioral claims about _mint_from_diffs, harness, slice.py, and other modules; none of that logic is in this chunk.
The _is_linked_worktree implementation is cut off at line 1-3; the structural inspection it promises is not visible.
_JUNK_KEYWORDS is all lowercase and excludes the specific words the comment says were previously misclassified (new, delete, default, case, switch, static, of, in).
_IDENTIFIER_RE uses \w which in Python 3 is unicode-aware by default, supporting the unicode claim.
_git catches OSError and subprocess.SubprocessError, which covers missing git, timeout, and subprocess failures; returncode check covers non-zero exits.
